..
A tropical anticyclone has situated itself over the Marianas, 
allowing light island showers to form along the axis of Guam and 
Saipan earlier this afternoon. While showers will remain minimal 
overnight as mostly clear skies develop. Light passing showers over 
the next few days will be followed by a return to a moderate trade- 
wind pattern sometime in the second half of the week, as a second 
high-pressure ridge moves in following a disintegrating Sinlaku well
north of Wake Island.

Marine...
Combined seas of 5 to 7 feet are expected to decrease another foot 
or two over the next few days as various distant swells weaken 
considerably. Even so, seas will remain choppy overnight as weaker 
pulses from distant Sinlaku continue to make their way across the 
region. A moderate risk of rip currents is expected along west, 
north, and east facing reefs of the Marianas tonight, to then drop to
low along west reefs Tuesday and persist through midweek. After, 
seas will begin to increase slowly toward the weekend as trade swell 
strengthens.

Eastern Micronesia...
A trade-wind trough moving along the ITCZ will continue to bring 
unsettled weather throughout much of eastern Micronesia through 
Tuesday. Scattered to numerous showers and isolated thunderstorms 
can be expected at all forecast points, including late this week and
into the weekend. A brief lull in shower and thunderstorm activity 
will be possible Wednesday into Thursday, though isolated to low-end 
scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms will still be possible. 
The ITCZ is forecast to dissipate late in the week and fragment into 
a series of trade- wind troughs that will continue the wet and 
unsettled weather across the region into the weekend. Though, a 
period or two of only isolated showers cannot be ruled out. Light to 
gentle variable winds will continue through Tuesday with east to 
northeast winds developing by Thursday. Winds will then increase to 
moderate to fresh as the pressure gradient tightens. Seas of 4 to 6 
feet will continue to subside through midweek and then increase late 
in the week as a northeast swell builds into eastern Micronesia.

Western Micronesia...
There were not a lot of changes needed for the inherited forecast. 
The main weather maker is a fragmented section of the Intertropical 
Convergence Zone (ITCZ) interacting with a few trade-wind troughs. 
This interaction is expected to produce scattered to numerous showers
for Chuuk State and is expected to gradually move westward over the 
next day or two. The next feature to move into this region is 
anticipated to be another section of the ITCZ with more embedded 
troughs in the latter half of the week. This is anticipated to bring 
more scattered showers to the region. Overall a wet week is in store 
for Chuuk. 

Over in Yap and Palau, a dry pattern regime has set up and is expected
to remain through much of the week. Showers may return near the end 
of the week as the troughs in Chuuk State make their way westward. 

Altimetry shows a plethora of combined sea heights across the 
region. Near Palau, seas are around 6 to 8 feet. For Yap, seas are 
around 7 to 9 feet. Finally for Chuuk, seas are around 4 to 6 feet. 
The elevated seas around Yap and Palau are due to the increased 
northeast swell being generated by distant Tropical Storm Sinlaku. 
As Sinlaku continues to move farther away from the region, this 
northeasterly swell is expected to continue to drop over the coming 
days. 

The surf at Yap is expected to be around 7 to 9 feet through tonight,
and expected to continue to fall over the next several days as the
trade swell re-estabilishes its dominance over the region and the
lunar cycle relaxes on the tides. Current estimations indicate the 
surf to fall below the 9 foot threshold of High Surf Advisory as 
early as Tuesday morning.
